haiku-low.q1: Nothing changes for them. Their linked sub signs them in via start_session. Google email changes are ignored, and the stored email is never updated.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter the correct password on the confirm page. Then the link is inserted, the pending link is deleted, and start_session runs.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. At 5 the account locks for 15 minutes, the pending link is deleted, and a locked message shows.
haiku-low.q4: No match: create a user with no password and verified email, insert the link, call start_session. Email not verified: refuse, point to email and password, create nothing.
haiku-low.q5: Error page, nothing changes. A callback after 10 minutes has an expired state, and a reloaded callback has a used state. Both get the error page.
haiku-low.q6: The existing single kind of session, via start_session. It replaces any old session and sets a new sid cookie, overwriting the browser's existing sid cookie.
haiku-low.q7: Neither is required. The signed-in user must match the user saved in the attempt. If that sub is linked to anyone else, the link is refused.
haiku-low.q8: In Redis, under the state value, for 10 minutes. The callback reads and deletes the entry once, or it is removed when it expires.
haiku-low.q9: Held in Redis, with user ID and sub, for 10 minutes. The browser holds only its random ID in a short-lived HttpOnly cookie. Success, lockout, or expiry deletes it.
haiku-low.q10: In the new Postgres table user_identities. Its UNIQUE constraints on user_id and sub enforce one Google account per user and one user per Google account.
haiku-low.q11: The user sees the error page and nothing changes. The exchange is not retried; the user must press the Google button again.
haiku-low.q12: The attempt entry records whether it started from login or settings. A settings link requires the signed-in user to match the saved user ID.

sonnet.q1: Nothing special: the callback finds the existing link by `sub`, and calls start_session for the linked user. The changed Google email does not matter and the stored email is never changed.
sonnet.q2: The user must confirm the account password. A pending link (sub, user ID) is saved in Redis for 10 minutes, with its ID in an HttpOnly cookie, and the confirm-password page is shown. Only after a correct password is the link inserted, failed_logins reset to 0, and start_session called. (If that user already has a different Google link, it is refused.)
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to failed_logins. At 5 the account is locked for 15 minutes (count resets to 0). The wrong password that triggers the lock deletes the pending link and shows the locked message. No link is created.
sonnet.q4: Verified email matching no user: create a user with no password and a verified email, insert the link, call start_session. If email_verified is false: refuse, point the user to email and password, and create nothing.
sonnet.q5: Error page and nothing changes. After 12 minutes the Redis entry (10-minute expiry) is gone, and a second load finds the entry already deleted, since the callback reads and deletes it once.
sonnet.q6: The same single kind of session as password login, created by start_session. It replaces any old session and sets the sid cookie, then redirects to `next` or /home.
sonnet.q7: No password is asked and the emails need not match. The signed-in user must be the one saved in the entry. If the sub is already linked to anyone else (or this user already has a Google link), it is refused (error page) and nothing is linked.
sonnet.q8: In Redis, keyed by the `state` value, with entry point, user ID and `next`. They are removed when the callback reads and deletes the entry in one step, or otherwise by the 10-minute expiry.
sonnet.q9: In Redis as a pending link (sub, user ID) with a 10-minute life. The browser refers to it by a short-lived HttpOnly cookie holding its random ID. It is deleted on success, on lockout, or on expiry.
sonnet.q10: In the new Postgres table user_identities(id, user_id, sub, created_at). The UNIQUE constraint on user_id gives one Google account per user, and the UNIQUE constraint on sub gives one user per Google account.
sonnet.q11: The user sees the error page and nothing is changed. There is no retry; the user presses the button again.
sonnet.q12: The Redis entry saved at start (looked up by `state`) records where the attempt started (login or settings) and, for settings, the user ID. For a settings link, the signed-in user must be the one saved in that entry, and the link is inserted for that user.
